method.docx_reader: python-docx with direct OOXML cross-check for the defective table
method.comparison_scope: Appendices A-W in the companion report against the corresponding workbook analytical sheets.
method.comparison_rule: For each appendix except K, join rows by an explicit stable identifier or composite identifier and compare only the columns represented in both artifacts. No fuzzy matching or row-position repair is used. Empty values normalize to empty strings; integer-valued spreadsheet numerics normalize to integer text; dates normalize to ISO date text.
method.kernel_table_cross_check: The report table immediately following paragraph 'K. Current v4.2 kernel requirements' was checked both through python-docx and directly in word/document.xml.
method.authority_rule: Cross-artifact parity establishes representational consistency between two S4 generated artifacts only. It does not independently validate the authoritative machine-readable source objects.

kernel_appendix_defect.title: Current v4.2 kernel requirements
kernel_appendix_defect.interpretation: The supplied report reserves 78 data rows for the kernel appendix but contains no cell text in those rows. The companion workbook contains the expected 78 populated kernel rows. This establishes a generated-report defect; it does not establish corruption of the authoritative KERNEL_REQUIREMENTS_v4.2.json object.

authority_label_discrepancy.observed_historical_claim: The report describes the companion Excel workbook as the canonical row-level analytical representation.
authority_label_discrepancy.successor_architecture_interpretation: Under the current programme store model, Excel and Word outputs are S4 generated views and machine-readable canonical records retain master-data authority.
authority_label_discrepancy.resolution_rule: Preserve the historical wording as immutable source evidence and record the successor authority interpretation explicitly; do not rewrite the predecessor report.

findings: Twenty-two of the twenty-three A-W appendices matched their corresponding workbook views exactly within the explicitly compared columns after stable-key joining: 1,376 rows and 11,617 field values, with zero missing keys, extra keys, or value mismatches.

Appendix K is the sole detected tabular representation defect in this bounded comparison: its 78 data rows contain 468 empty data cells even though the companion workbook has 78 populated kernel rows across the six represented columns.
Direct OOXML inspection of appendix K found only the six header text nodes in that table, confirming that the empty body is not a python-docx text-extraction artifact.

The defect is confined by current evidence to the generated report representation. No claim is made that KERNEL_REQUIREMENTS_v4.2.json, the workbook Kernel_Requirements sheet, or the v4.2 normative kernel is corrupted.
The report's historical authority wording for the workbook conflicts with the successor S1-S5 store model and is preserved as a recorded authority-label discrepancy rather than silently rewritten.
